To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate a photon shot-noire-limited optical magnetometer with sub picotesla sensitivity at ambient temperatures, using a rubidium vapor cell with anti-relaxed coating, and that we demonstrate the shot-noise-limits by scaling of the noise with optical power in agreement with theoretical prediction.
we demonstrate a room-temperature, photon-shot-noise-limited, optical magnetometer with a sensitivity of 70fT/√Hz at 7 μT, and that the noise scales with optical power as predicted by theory.
a room-temperature optical magnetometer has been developed that is shot-noise limited and that achieves a sensitivity of 70 fT / √Hz.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of optical magnetometers.
the development of new methods of measuring the magnetic field.

the development of a new generation of magnetometers based on atomic vapors and laser light, which will be used for a wide range of applications in the field of geophysics and geology, medicine and biology, as well as for fundamental research in the field of quantum metrology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated a room-temperature SNL optical magnetometer with sub-pT sensitivity.

this paper presents an important step forward towards the realisation of a room-temperature, shot-noise limited magnetometer with sub-pT sensitivity, and that this is an exciting development for future applications of optical magnetometers.
we report a photon shot noise-limited (SN) optical magnetometer with sub-pT/√Hz sensitivity at room temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the best room-temperature magnetometer sensitivity to date.
we have achieved a room-temperature SNL magnetometer with sub picotesla sensitivity.
we are the first to demonstrate a SNL magnetometer with sub-pT/√Hz sensitivity at room temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensitivity of the magnetometer can be improved significantly by reducing relaxation of the Rb atoms in the vapor cell.
SNL magnetometers based on amplitude modulating optical rotation can be built using room-temperature vapors, and that the performance is not limited by relaxation or diffusion of polarized atoms.
SNL magnetometers can be operated at room temperature, with a sensitivity that is only limited by the photon shot noise.
